title: Sounding out short words one sound at a time
examples: How do I sound out a word?

explain.say: Imagine a word is a little train. Each carriage holds one sound. Look at the word cat on the board. Let us ride the train together, one carriage at a time.

draw.text: Sounding out short words one sound at a time

explain.say: Look at the first part lighting up. It is the letter c. Here it makes the first sound in kite. Tap your shoulder and say that sound. Can you say it with me?
Now the middle part glows. It is a, the first sound in apple. Tap your elbow and say it. Lovely! Two taps, two sounds.
Last part: t, the first sound in tiger. Tap your hand. Three taps for three sounds. Now say them faster and faster. Can you hear the word cat pop out?
You did it, you read a word! Your brain learns in its own way, and lots of brilliant people learn like this. Now try the word with the sun. Tap each sound, then blend. What word is it?

faq.a: It means saying each sound in a word, one at a time. Then you push the sounds together until you hear the word.
asks: How do I sound out a word?

faq.q: Why do I tap my arm?
faq.a: Tapping gives each sound its own place. Your hands and ears work together, and that helps the sounds stick.
Blending means joining sounds together. Say them again and again, a bit faster each time, until they melt into one word.
asks: How do I join the sounds?

faq.q: What if I get a sound wrong?
faq.a: That is fine, everybody does. Go back to the first sound and try again, nice and steady. A teacher or grown-up can say the sounds with you.

faq.q: Which words are best to start with?
faq.a: Start with three-letter words like cat, sun, pig, hop and bed. Each letter makes one sound, so they are perfect for practice.

facts: The word cat has three letters and three sounds.
Words like cat, sun and pig are often called CVC words: consonant, vowel, consonant.

quiz.say: How many sounds are in the word sun?
quiz.show: How many sounds are in sun?
quiz.why: Sun has three sounds, one for each letter: s, u and n.

wrong.0: There is one more. Tap them and you get three taps.
wrong.2: Sun has only three letters, and each one makes one sound.

quiz.say: After you say each sound, what do you do next?
quiz.show: After saying each sound, what next?
quiz.why: You push the sounds together, faster and faster, until you hear the word.

wrong.1: Guessing can trick you. Blending the sounds tells you the real word.
wrong.2: No need to skip. Blending the sounds helps you read it.
